propositions: Patch-set upload events are permanently dropped by the reconciler when the cursor advances to newest event time without recording a low-water mark, causing changes to stall unvoted and unreachable in all future reconcile passes.

Gerrit webhook delivers at-most-once (not at-least-once), and dropped events are only recoverable if the reconciler re-drives them, which fails silently when a candidate is not voted in the first pass that sees it.
The cursor must be clamped to the minimum of newest event and oldest retryably-abandoned candidate to re-admit stalled changes in subsequent passes.

Terminal outcomes (skipped with certain reasons, voted changes) must advance the cursor, while retryable states (error, deferred, reconcile_check_error, review_timeout) must hold it back, bounded by RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS to prevent permanent pinning.

Queue depth, held-back candidate tracking, and reconcile_done observability must be exposed via /health and structured logging so operators can distinguish bot-down, running, queued, and dropped states.
